descript.abstract: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) has compiled a geodatabase containing mineral-related geospatial data for the People's Republic of China. The data can be used in analyses of the extractive fuel and nonfuel mineral industries and related economic and physical infrastructure integral for the successful operation of the mineral industries within the area of study as well as the movement of mineral products across domestic and global markets. This geodatabase reflects the USGS ongoing commitment to its mission of understanding the nature and distribution of global mineral commodity supply chains by updating and publishing the georeferenced locations of mineral commodity production and processing facilities, mineral exploration and development sites, and mineral commodity exporting ports for the countries in the area of study. The geodatabase contains data feature classes from USGS, foreign governmental, and open-source sources as follows: (1) mineral production and processing facilities, (2) mineral exploration and development sites, (3) mineral occurrence sites and deposits, (4) undiscovered mineral resource tracts for antimony, copper, phosphate, and potash, (5) coal occurrence areas, (6) electric power generating facilities, (7) electric power transmission lines, (8) liquefied natural gas terminals, (9) undiscovered, technically recoverable conventional and continuous hydrocarbon resources (by USGS geologic province), (10) cumulative production and recoverable conventional resources (by province groups), and (11) major mineral exporting maritime ports.
descript.purpose: The primary goal of this project was to compile a range of geospatial data feature classes in this ArcGIS (ESRI) geodatabase that can be used in analyses of the extractive fuel and nonfuel mineral industries and the related economic and physical infrastructure in the People's Republic of China, which are integral for the successful operation of the mineral industries within the region and the transportation of mineral products across domestic and global markets.

idinfo.useconst: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) provides these geographic data "as is." Unless otherwise stated, all data, metadata and related materials are considered to satisfy the quality standards relative to the purpose for which the data were collected. Although these data and associated metadata have been processed successfully on USGS computer systems, reviewed for accuracy and completeness, and approved for release by the USGS, no warranty expressed or implied is made regarding the display or utility of the data on any other system or for general or scientific purposes, nor shall the act of distribution constitute any such warranty. The burden for determining fitness for use of these data lies entirely with the user. Users are advised to read the dataset's metadata thoroughly to understand appropriate use and data limitations.
idinfo.datacred: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), National Minerals Information Center (https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center). These data were collected, formatted for use within a geographic information system, and standardized as part of an overview of mineral-related geospatial information on the People's Republic of China. Data were compiled from various sources including USGS publications, foreign government reports and publications, peer-reviewed journal articles, and digital mineral databases, as documented within the "Credits" and lineage sections of the metadata for each individual feature class in this geodatabase.

attracc.attraccr: All feature attribute values were peer reviewed for accuracy. Values were checked for correct data type and for presence / absence. Where possible, geographical location coordinates were checked on satellite imagery for accuracy.

dataqual.logic: Data quality assurance and data quality control logic tests were performed for several feature classes. However, as many feature classes are directly from authoritative sources or from previously published governmental or scientific work, not all layers were subjected to a new logical accuracy test. Visual comparison of the feature classes supports the robustness of the overall data for feature classes not created by the National Minerals Information Center or from other programs within the U.S. Geological Survey.
dataqual.complete: Data set is considered complete for the information presented, as described in the abstract. Users are advised to read the rest of the metadata records, including data-level metadata records, carefully for additional details.

horizpa.horizpar: All relevant feature geometry was reviewed against satellite imagery in Google Earth (TM) or ESRI Global Satellite Imagery where not obtained from authoritative sources. Each individual feature class includes fields on locational accuracy and these fields should be checked for additional reference as to positional accuracy on a feature-by-feature basis.

vertacc.vertaccr: No formal positional accuracy tests were conducted.

procstep.procdesc: Surveys of relevant foreign governmental mining and petroleum agencies, ministries, and scientific counterpart agencies were conducted to assess their geospatial data holdings. Three data feature classes were created by NMIC researchers using NMIC / USGS data as well as extensive research into individual operations: mineral extraction and processing facilities, mineral exploration sites, and mineral commodity exporting ports of the region. In addition, four data feature classes were created by NMIC researchers using regional- and/or country-level NMIC / USGS data: oil and gas undiscovered conventional resources (by geologic province), oil and gas undiscovered conventional resources (by geologic province group), oil and gas undiscovered continuous resources (by geologic province), and oil and gas recoverable resources and cumulative production (by country). Data were assembled into geodatabase-normalized formats for use within the GIS and geospatial PDF map product. Additional geospatial data, such as tracts of undiscovered mineral resource assessments, land transportation and energy infrastructure, cartographic elements (rivers, lakes), and political / administrative boundaries were imported from external sources in geodatabase-normalized formats with some modifications as outlined in the database-level metadata files for each feature class. These modifications included re-labeling feature attributes to fit our GIS attributes table schema, excluding data not relevant for the purpose of the GIS product (e.g. features outside the area of interest), or merging features for ease of displaying them in the final GIS and geospatial PDF map product.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of selected dams in China. Data for each facility were obtained from multiple sources, including the Global Energy Observatory, the Chinese National Committee on Large Dams, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Registry, Nature Conservancy Dam Impact database, and the World Wide Dams Technical Data and Detailed Specs. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data. *Note: There are several entries in the source database that lack geographical coordinate locations (Latitude and Longitude) but contain other data that are of value for this geodatabase (e.g. qualitative location, installed capacity, controlling authority, equity holders), which may be used to assess the energy capacity of different countries in the study area. As such, we have included those data in this geodatabase.

enttyp.enttypl: China Electrical Power Generating Stations (GIS Feature Class)
enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the power-generating stations that were operational, in rehabilitation, or had idle capacity in China in 2021. Data for each facility were obtained from multiple sources, including the global coal power plant tracker, the Chinese National Committee on Large Dams, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Registry, and the global energy observatory. Power stations were categorized by the USGS into “Capacity Range” groups according to their installed capacity (in megawatts, if known) and “Fuel Categories” based on the type of fuel(s) consumed in the generation of electricity. Fuel categories include Renewable (solar, wind, hydro, biomass, and geothermal), Non-Renewable (diesel, fuel oils including crude and heavy fuel oil, and natural gas), and Other/Unknown for those where facility data is insufficient for categorization. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.*Note: There are several entries in the source database that lack geographical coordinate locations (Latitude and Longitude) but contain other data that are of value for this geodatabase (e.g. qualitative location, installed capacity, controlling authority, equity holders), which may be used to assess the energy capacity of different regions or provinces in the study area. As such, we have included those data in this geodatabase.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the Extra high voltage and ultra high voltage power transmission lines in China in 2018. Transmission lines were categorized by the USGS into “Voltage Classification” groups according to their transmission voltages (in kilovolts). The groups are based on the classifications generally used in the global energy industry (e.g. U.S. Department of Energy, 2015, United States Electricity Industry Primer, Fig. 15; https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2015/12/f28/united-states-electricity-industry-primer.pdf): Extra High Voltage (EHV) = >275 kV and Ultra High Voltage (UHV) = >765 kV. Data was obtained from the State Grid Corporation of China, China Electric Power Planning & engineering Institute, and China Energy Research Association.

enttyp.enttypl: China Infrastructure Mineral Commodity Exporting Ports (GIS Feature Class)
enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of 374 fuel and non-fuel mineral commodity exporting ports in China compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s National Minerals Information Center. The dataset provides some generalized information about each port, or terminal operations within a port, such as name of the port or terminal, mineral commodity(ies) exported, exporting capacity, source and(or) destination of commodities, and operator/ownership, if available. Sources of information used to compile this dataset include the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's World Port Index (WPI) report, U.S. Energy Information Administration country profiles, China maps, digital global mapping services, company and port authority reports and websites, company press releases, global industry reports, and government reports. The data are not comprehensive and are intended to highlight the general distribution of mineral commodity exporting ports in Africa and their connectivity to other transportation infrastructure across China. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source(s) to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

The dataset provides some generalized information about each exploration project, such as project name, ownership, mineral commodity(ies), exploration status, year of last known activity, and location descriptions. Note that the accuracy of locations is highly variable due to the lack of detailed information for many exploration projects. For instances in which little information beyond the name, commodity, and generalized location of an exploration site is known or available, we assigned the centroid coordinates (low accuracy) of the first level administrative region (ADM1, if available).

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of 2,424 fuel and non-fuel mineral production and processing operations in China compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s (USGS) National Minerals Information Center. The dataset provides some generalized information about each mineral operation, such as name of the operation or facility, mineral commodity(ies) produced or processed, status (as of 2019), capacity, operator/ownership, and location descriptions. Non-GIS data were derived from Table 2 of individual country chapters published in the USGS 2019 Minerals Yearbook, Vol. III (Area Reports: International) publication. All data were reorganized and restructured from their original format to fit our GIS attributes table format, updated for accuracy when additional information was available, and georeferenced for this geodatabase using various sources that included company documents (annual reports, press releases, etc.), scientific/geologic reports, industry reports, government reports, maps, digital mapping services, and minerals- and mining-specific databases, as noted for each record. The data are intended to highlight the state of the minerals industries in China as of 2019.

Phosphate rock is utilized worldwide for the manufacture of phosphoric acid and various types of chemical fertilizers. The permissive tracts represent either the areal extent of, or surface projection of rocks with occurrences of phosphate mineralization or potential deposits in which phosphate may be present. The dataset was created by the U.S. Geological Survey as part of a larger study to identify the potential for phosphate deposits in Afghanistan and adjacent countries, including parts of China, and published by its original authors as USGS Open-File Report 2015-1121. In this feature class, all polygons that delineate permissive tracts entirely outside of our study area were excluded, some attributes were excluded or summarized, and the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

enttyp.enttypl: China Mineral Resource Assessment of Potash (GIS Feature Class)
enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains information on potash geology in the form of polygons that represent permissive tracts for evaporite-related potash-bearing stratabound salt and potash-bearing halokinetic salt deposits in China. Potash, as used in this report, refers to potassium-bearing minerals, ores, and processed products. Glauconite and alunite deposits as sources of potash were not considered during the assessment. The permissive tracts represent either the areal extent of, or surface projection of rocks within the upper 3 km of the Earth’s crust where undiscovered deposits of potash may be present. The dataset was created for the U.S. Geological Survey Global Mineral Resource Assessment Project (GMRAP), and published by its original authors as USGS Scientific Investigations Series Report 2010-5090-S. The primary objectives of the project are to outline the principal areas that have potential for selected undiscovered mineral resources and to estimate the probable amounts of those mineral resources to a depth of 1-3 kilometers below the earth's surface. In this layer, all polygons that delineate permissive tracts entirely outside of the study area were excluded, some attributes were excluded or summarized, and the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

enttyp.enttypl: China Oil and Gas Recoverable Resources and Cumulative Production (GIS Feature Class)
enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains data for cumulative production and total recoverable proven plus probable resources of conventional and continuous hydrocarbon resources in oil fields and in gas fields within China. Data are stored as polygon attributes, summarized by region (provinces, administrative areas, and offshore regions) as hydrocarbon resources in oil fields, in gas fields, and total including a BOE [barrel of oil equivalent = oil + NGL + gas (BCF/6)] (NGL = natural gas liquids). Units are million barrels of oil (MMBO), millions of barrels of natural gas liquids (MMBNGL), billion cubic feet gas (BCFG), and millions of barrels of oil equivalent (MMBOE). With the exception of total number of fields, data are rounded to no more than three significant digits and may not add to totals shown. Data denoted as "-111.111" are withheld to conceal proprietary data. Null entries (no data) are denoted as "-999.999." The Chinese Exclusive Economic Zone boundary is included as a polygon feature for the sole purpose of visually illustrating offshore resources in our dataset. The following footnote is included in the attributes table under the "Footnotes (MemoOther)" field: Offshore resources are reported separately from onshore and may be located outside the Chinese Exclusive Economic Zone. Total resources in the area of study are included in a separate polygon encompassing the country boundaries for China and are inclusive of offshore resources.
